cast.name: THE MAN IN THE BROWN COAT
names: THE MAN IN THE BROWN COAT

units.text: INT. FOOD TRUCK - CONTINUOUS
Narrow and hot.
BIG DAVE, 50s, wide shoulders, works the grill.
JEN, 30s, takes orders at the window.
MO, 20s, is cutting limes and does not talk much.
SAM, 30s, a quiet man in a clean jacket, sits on a milk crate near the back with a paper cup of coffee.
Okay, team. Three pork, two fish, one no onions. Mo, the no-onions one is for the old lady.
units.name: JEN

units.text: Okay.
units.name: MO

units.text: The old lady always want extra sauce. She says it is for her health.
units.name: BIG DAVE

units.text: Dave, her health is fine. She just likes sauce.
units.name: JEN

units.text: Sam lifts his cup.
He watches the street.
A grey car is parked across the road for the second day.
Same car. Same man.
units.name: SAM

units.text: Sam, you say something?
units.name: JEN

units.text: No. Nothing. I talk to the coffee.
units.name: SAM

units.text: The coffee is the best listener in the truck.
units.name: BIG DAVE

units.text: A phone BUZZES on the shelf above the grill.
Big Dave wipes his hands on his apron and picks it up.
Hello? Yes. Yes, this is Dave.
units.name: BIG DAVE

units.text: David, it is Mrs. Kowalczyk from the corner. Is my delivery ready? My grandson is coming at one o'clock and he is very hungry.
units.name: MRS. K

units.text: Yes, Mrs. K. Twelve tacos, wrapped, in the back. Mo will bring them in ten minutes.
units.name: BIG DAVE

units.text: You are a good boy. Tell Jen she needs a husband.
units.name: MRS. K

units.text: I heard that!
units.name: JEN

units.text: Big Dave puts the phone down, smiling.
Mo slides the limes into a plastic tub.
You are looking at the car again.
units.name: MO

units.text: Maybe I am.
units.name: SAM

units.text: Is not our business. We make tacos.
units.name: MO

units.text: You are right. We make tacos.
units.name: SAM

units.text: A customer, a TEENAGE GIRL in headphones, steps to the window and puts down a ten-dollar bill.
Hi. What can I make for you?
units.name: JEN

units.text: Just two. Anything.
units.name: TEENAGE GIRL

units.text: Two pork, Dave!
units.name: JEN

units.text: Two pork. Always pork. Nobody is brave anymore.
units.name: BIG DAVE

units.text: Outside, the grey car's door opens.
A man in a brown coat gets out and crosses the road slowly, hands in his pockets.
Everyone. Stay calm. Keep working.
units.name: SAM
paren: standing, setting down his cup, soft

units.text: What is happening?
units.name: JEN

units.text: Maybe nothing. Maybe a man wants a taco.
units.name: SAM

units.text: The man arrives at the window.
He looks past Jen, past the grill, and finds Sam.
Hello, Sam. It has been a long time.
units.name: THE MAN IN THE BROWN COAT

units.text: Yes. A long time, Inspector.
units.name: SAM

units.text: Inspector. Of course. The one day I forget the napkins.
units.name: BIG DAVE

units.text: Is this a joke?
units.name: JEN

units.text: I think no.
units.name: MO

units.text: The man puts a business card on the counter.
Jen reads it without touching it.
Do not worry. I am not here for the truck. I only wish to talk. Five minutes. Then I eat, and then I go.
units.name: THE MAN IN THE BROWN COAT

units.text: Dave. Please keep my coffee warm.
units.name: SAM
paren: taking off his apron, folding it neatly

units.text: The coffee will wait. It is a patient coffee.
units.name: BIG DAVE

units.text: Sam steps out of the back door.
The man in the brown coat holds it for him.
They walk down the street together, slowly, the way old friends walk, or old enemies.
Okay. Does anyone know what just happened?
units.name: JEN
paren: to Mo, to Dave, to the air

units.text: No.
units.name: MO

units.text: Two pork for the girl. Then we will see.
units.name: BIG DAVE

units.text: Jen sighs and wipes the counter.
The line shuffles forward.
The sun keeps shining, and the onions keep sizzling, as if nothing in the world had changed at all.
A phone BUZZES again on the shelf.
Nobody picks it up.
